seo.metaDescription: Injured in a Poway car accident? Get a free consultation with an attorney serving Rt 67, Poway Road, and Pomerado Road.

hero.subtitle: If a crash on Poway Road or Route 67 left you hurt, we can help you understand your options at no cost. Our team handles San Diego County car accident claims.

about.title: Poway Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Poway's mix of state route traffic and busy local corridors like Pomerado Road and Twin Peaks Road creates real risk for drivers, especially during the Wednesday evening rush between 5 and 7 p.m. when public crash records show reported collisions tend to cluster. In a recent year, San Diego County recorded 70 injury collisions in Poway alone, with 95 people hurt and 5 lives lost. If you were injured in one of these crashes, the period right after matters. Insurance adjusters often call quickly, hoping for a recorded statement before you've had time to understand your injuries or talk to anyone. We handle car accident claims directly and can help you evaluate the crash, preserve evidence like dashcam footage or skid patterns, and explain your options under California law.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Speaking With an Insurer

items.title: California's Comparative Fault Rule
items.desc: California allows you to recover damages even if you're partly at fault, but your share of fault reduces the recovery. We can help make sure fault is assessed fairly rather than accepted at face value from the other driver's insurer.

items.title: The Clock Starts Ticking Fast
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a car accident lawsuit, but claims involving a government-owned road or vehicle can require notice in as little as six months. Knowing which timeline applies to your Poway crash matters early on.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: California doesn't limit compensation for pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life in a standard car accident case. We can help make sure these harms are properly documented and valued, not just your medical bills.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers sometimes use early statements, made before you know the full extent of your injuries, to minimize what they later offer. We can advise you on how to respond to insurer requests.

items.question: What if my crash happened on Route 67 and involved a Caltrans-maintained road issue?
items.answer: If a government entity's road design or maintenance played a role, California requires a claim notice be filed much sooner than the standard two-year window, sometimes within six months. This is one reason it helps to talk with us quickly after a crash on a state route like Route 67.

items.question: Is there a cost to hire us?
items.answer: There is no charge for a free consultation. We typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation.
